APIs.APIs_DESC: This section lists all the APIs of the MCALLIB driver.

API.API_SAFETY_LEVEL: Refer to the release notes for the safety related info

API_RETURN.API_PARAMDESC: The return from the macro is the 32-bit CRC value

API_IN.API_PARAMDESC: Initial seed value or the cumulative CRC result from a previous sequence of data. This input parameter supports 32 bits value.
Value for which CRC needs to be calculated. This input parameter supports 32 bits value.

API.API_DESC: CRC32 is provided as macro that calculates the CRC of four bytes of data in big-endian order which is provided as input. Note: CRC32 is used by other modules of MCAL. Compiler abstraction for instruction based CRC is provided by MCALLIB. The syntax of assembly instruction used in CRC32 is compiler dependent and hence, MCALLIB uses compiler specific switches to support multiple compilers.
API.API_AUTOSAR_VERSION: Applicable for Autosar versions 4.2.2, 4.4.0 and R24-11.

API.API_SAFETY_LEVEL: Refer to the release notes for the safety related info

API_RETURN.API_PARAMDESC: Indicates the calculated CRC for 32-bit register

API_IN.API_PARAMDESC: Initial seed value or the cumulative CRC result from a previous sequence of data. This input parameter supports 32 bits value.
Value for which CRC needs to be calculated. This input parameter supports 8 bits value.

API.API_DESC: CRC32B is provided as macro that calculates the CRC of one byte of data which is provided as input. Note: CRC32B is used by other modules of MCAL. Compiler abstraction for instruction based CRC32B is provided by MCALLIB. The syntax of assembly instruction used in CRC32B is compiler dependent and hence, MCALLIB uses compiler specific switches to support multiple compilers.
API.API_AUTOSAR_VERSION: Applicable for Autosar versions 4.2.2, 4.4.0 and R24-11.

API.API_SAFETY_LEVEL: Refer to the release notes for the safety related info

API_RETURN.API_PARAMDESC: The result from the macro is the calculated CRC.

API_IN.API_PARAMDESC:
Indicates the configuration based on which the CRC would be calculated:
- Bit 0 to 2 indicates the input data width in the range [1-8]. - Bit 3 to 7 is unused and must be 0 - Bit 8 indicates the data bit order. 0 is big endian, 1 is little endian - Bit 9 indicates application of logical inversion to result and initial value. - Bit 10 to 11 is unused and must be 0 - Bit 12 to 15 contains the width of the input data in the range range [1-16] - Bit 16 to 31 indicates the Polynomial value to be supported for the CRC calculation
This input parameter supports 32 bits value.
Indicates the data for which CRC is to be calculated. This input parameter supports 8 bits value.
Indicates initial seed value or the cumulative CRC result from a previous sequence of data. This input parameter supports 16 bits value.

API.API_DESC: CRCN is provided as a macro that calculates the CRC of 1 to 8-bits on the input data. Note: Compiler abstraction for instruction based CRC is provided by MCALLIB. The syntax of assembly instruction used in CRCN is compiler dependent and hence, MCALLIB uses compiler specific switches to support multiple compilers.
API.API_AUTOSAR_VERSION: Applicable for Autosar versions 4.2.2, 4.4.0 and R24-11.

API.API_SAFETY_LEVEL: Refer to the release notes for the safety related info
API.API_DESC: The DSYNC is a memory barrier instruction, enforces all data accesses associated with the instructions are completed. Note: The syntax of assembly instruction used in DSYNC compiler dependent and hence, MCALLIB uses compiler specific switches to support multiple compilers.
API.API_AUTOSAR_VERSION: Applicable for Autosar versions 4.2.2, 4.4.0 and R24-11.

API.API_SAFETY_LEVEL: Refer to the release notes for the safety related info

API_RETURN.API_PARAMDESC: The macro returns the extracted data from the value provided. The data returned is of unsigned integer type.

API_IN.API_PARAMDESC: Indicates the value (32-bit) from which the bits need to be extracted. This input parameter supports 32 bits value.
Indicates the bit offset from LSB. This input parameter supports 32 bits value.
Indicates the number of bits to be extracted. This input parameter supports 32 bits value.

API.API_DESC: EXTRACT is provided as macro that may be used to extract required number of bits of data from a given value. Note: EXTRACT is used by MCALLIB and other modules of MCAL. Compiler abstraction for instruction based EXTRACT is provided by MCALLIB. The syntax of assembly instruction used in EXTRACT is compiler dependent and hence, MCALLIB uses compiler specific switches to support multiple compilers.
API.API_AUTOSAR_VERSION: Applicable for Autosar versions 4.2.2, 4.4.0 and R24-11.

API.API_SAFETY_LEVEL: Refer to the release notes for the safety related info

API_RETURN.API_PARAMDESC: The function writes the number of bits of an integer value at a certain address location in memory with a bitoffset.

API_IN.API_PARAMDESC: Address of the variable to be updated(32-bit aligned). This input parameter supports 32 bits value.
Value which needs to be written. This input parameter supports 32 bits value.
Bit offset from LSB. This input parameter supports 32 bits value.
Number of bits to be modified from Offset. This input parameter supports 32 bits value.

API.API_DESC: IMASKLDMST is provided as macro that atomically updates required bits in a 32-bit value. Note: IMASKLDMST is used by MCALLIB and other modules of MCAL. Compiler abstraction for instruction based IMASKLDMST is provided by MCALLIB. The syntax of assembly instruction used in IMASKLDMST is compiler dependent and hence, MCALLIB uses compiler specific switches to support multiple compilers.
API.API_AUTOSAR_VERSION: Applicable for Autosar versions 4.2.2, 4.4.0 and R24-11.

API.API_SAFETY_LEVEL: Refer to the release notes for the safety related info
API.API_DESC: The ISYNC is an instruction barrier. Enforces all instructions are completed prior to ISYNC and flushes the instruction pipeline. Note: The syntax of assembly instruction used in ISYNC is compiler dependent and hence, MCALLIB uses compiler specific switches to support multiple compilers.
API.API_AUTOSAR_VERSION: Applicable for Autosar versions 4.2.2, 4.4.0 and R24-11.

API.API_SAFETY_LEVEL: Refer to the release notes for the safety related info

API_RETURN.API_PARAMDESC: The macro returns initial value of the 1st input parameter.

API_IN.API_PARAMDESC: Address of the variable. This input parameter supports 32 bits value.
Value to be swapped. This input parameter supports 32 bits value.
Value to be compared. This input parameter supports 32 bits value.

API.API_DESC: The Mcal_CmpAndSwap is provided as a macro which is used to swaps the content of 1st input parameter with the value of the 2nd input parameter, if the contents at the 1st input parameter is equal to that of 3rd input parameter. Note: Mcal_CmpAndSwap is used by MCALLIB and other modules of MCAL. Compiler abstraction for instruction based Mcal_CmpAndSwap is provided by MCALLIB. The syntax of assembly instruction used in Mcal_CmpAndSwap is compiler dependent and hence, MCALLIB uses compiler specific switches to support multiple compilers.
API.API_AUTOSAR_VERSION: Applicable for Autosar versions 4.2.2, 4.4.0 and R24-11.

API_RETURN.API_PARAMDESC: This macro returns the number of leading zeros.

API_IN.API_PARAMDESC: Variable whose leading zero needs to be counted. This input parameter supports 32 bits value.

API.API_DESC: Mcal_CountLeadingZeros is provided as macro and used to count the number of consecutive leading zeros in the value provided starting with bit 31. Note: Mcal_CountLeadingZeros is used by other modules of MCAL. Compiler abstraction for instruction based Mcal_CountLeadingZeros is provided by MCALLIB. The syntax of assembly instruction used in Mcal_CountLeadingZeros is compiler dependent and hence, MCALLIB uses compiler specific switches to support multiple compilers.
API.API_AUTOSAR_VERSION: Applicable for Autosar versions 4.2.2, 4.4.0 and R24-11.

API.API_SAFETY_LEVEL: Refer to the release notes for the safety related info

API_RETURN.API_PARAMDESC: This function is a implementation of a binary semaphore using swap instruction

API_IN.API_PARAMDESC: Address of the variable to be swapped.This input parameter supports 32 bits value.
Value to be swapped.This input parameter supports 32 bits value.
Mask which indicates the bits that need to be updated.This input parameter supports 32 bits value.

API.API_DESC: The Mcal_Swap is provided as a macro and used to swap two values based on a mask. Note: Mcal_Swap is used by modules of MCAL. Compiler abstraction for instruction based Mcal_Swap is provided by MCALLIB. The syntax of assembly instruction used in Mcal_Swap is compiler dependent and hence, MCALLIB uses compiler specific switches to support multiple compilers.

API_RETURN.API_PARAMDESC: Contents of the addressed Core Specific Function Register (CSFR) is moved into a data register.

API_IN.API_PARAMDESC: Indicates address from the CSFR base address of the executing core. This input parameter supports 32 bits value.

API_RETURN.API_PARAMDESC: Contents of the passed data is moved to the addressed Core Specific Function Register (CSFR).

API_IN.API_PARAMDESC: Indicates address from the CSFR base address of the executing core. This input parameter supports 32 bits value.
Data to be moved. This input parameter supports 32 bits value.

API.API_SYNTAX: void Mcal_WriteSafetyEndInitProtReg16 ( void * const RegAddress, const uint16 DataValue )
API.API_SAFETY_LEVEL: Refer to the release notes for the safety related info

API_OUT.API_PARAMDESC: Safety Endinit protected register address having 16 bit access Note: The pointer will be pointer to volatile since the address passed is of a register.

API_IN.API_PARAMDESC: Value to be written to the register located at RegAddress.

API.API_DESC: The API unlocks the safety ENDINIT protection, updates the protected register with 16-bit accesses and then locks back the safety ENDINIT protection. The API writes the value specified in 'DataValue' into the safety ENDINIT protected register, whose address is specified in 'RegAddress'.
API.API_AUTOSAR_VERSION: Applicable for Autosar versions 4.2.2, 4.4.0 and R24-11.

API.API_SAFETY_LEVEL: Refer to the release notes for the safety related info

API_OUT.API_PARAMDESC: Address for the safety ENDINIT protected register. Note: The pointer will be pointer to volatile since the address passed is of a register.

API_IN.API_PARAMDESC: Value to be written to the register located at RegAddress.
Mask value for updating the registers. Bits set as 1 in the mask, will be updated in 'RegAddress', all the other bits are unchanged.

API.API_DESC: The API updates the safety ENDINIT protected register, for which the address is specified by 'RegAddress'. The API also supports write access to safety endinit protected CSFRs, for which the 16-bit offset is specified by 'RegAddress'. The register is updated with the corresponding data value for the bit position where the mask value is 1. The remaining bits retain their original value. If register address is null pointer, then a safety error is reported. The API disables the safety ENDINIT protection, updates the protected register and then enables the safety ENDINIT protection.
API.API_AUTOSAR_VERSION: Applicable for Autosar versions 4.2.2, 4.4.0 and R24-11.

API.API_AUTOSAR_VERSION: Applicable for Autosar versions 4.2.2, 4.4.0 and R24-11.

API.API_SAFETY_LEVEL: Refer to the release notes for the safety related info

API_RETURN.API_PARAMDESC: System timer (STM) resolution: Value of 1 STM tick in nano seconds.

API.API_DESC: The API is invoked by the MCU driver to indicate to the MCALLIB driver, that the clock tree is updated. As a result of invocation of the API, the MCALLIB driver takes the following actions: - Calculates the STM resolution based on the new clock tree. - Old STM resolution is updated with the newly calculated value within the library. Note: The API is expected to be invoked only by the MCU driver, which is responsible for configuring the clock tree.
API.USER_HINTS: The MCU clock tree should be initialized prior calling the API. The API is allowed to be called only by the MCAL MCU driver. Note: In the flowchart, the value of Ndiv,Pdiv,K2 div are NDIV+1,PDIV+1(from SYSPLLCON0 register) and K2DIV+1(from SYSPLLCON1 register respectively) Note: In the flowchart, the value of TIMER_RESOL_1_NANOSEC is 10^9, which is used to return STM timer resolution in 1ns resolution.
API.API_AUTOSAR_VERSION: Applicable for Autosar versions 4.2.2, 4.4.0 and R24-11.

API.API_SAFETY_LEVEL: Refer to the release notes for the safety related info

API_RETURN.API_PARAMDESC: System timer(STM) resolution: Value of 1 STM tick in nano second.

API.API_DESC: The API retrieves the resolution of a STM in nanosecond. Note: A return value of 0 indicates that STM is switched off or the Mcal_DelayResetTickCalibration API was never invoked.
API.API_AUTOSAR_VERSION: Applicable for Autosar versions 4.2.2, 4.4.0 and R24-11.

API_IN.API_PARAMDESC: Value of the variable or register from which bits need to extracted.
Starting bit position of the data to be extracted.
Bit length of the data to be extracted.

Bit length of the data to be modified
Value to be updated to address pointed by DataPtr

Only the bits specified by BitPos and BitLen is updated, all the other bits are unchanged. Note: The API is implemented as a macro.

API.API_DESC: The API returns the global address of a local PSPR address of the specified CPU.

API.API_SYNTAX: void Mcal_GetSpinlock ( volatile uint32 * const LockAddress, const uint32 Timeout )
API.API_SAFETY_LEVEL: Refer to the release notes for the safety related info

API_IN.API_PARAMDESC: Address of the spinlock to be acquired.
Maximum wait time(micro second) to acquire the spinlock.

API.API_DESC: The API acquires the passed spinlock atomically. It is implemented in MCALLIB using Test, Test and Set Spinlock (TTAS) mechanism. A Timeout shall be passed as input parameter to spinlock API so that TTAS does not enter into an indefinite loop. If spinlock is not acquired within the specified timeout, then the control returns to the application after reporting a safety error. Note: If the STM frequency and the value of Mcal_StmTimerResolution are guaranteed by the user to remain unchanged across all cores during spinlock operations, then Mcal_GetSpinlock may be safely used as a re-entrant API.
API.USER_HINTS: User shall ensure that when this interface is used the McalLibSafetyEnable parameter shall be enabled to detect timeout.
API.API_AUTOSAR_VERSION: Applicable for Autosar versions 4.2.2, 4.4.0 and R24-11.

CONTAINER.CONTAINER_DESC: Container for all the general configuration parameters for the MCALLIB driver.

PARAMETER.PARAM_DESC: Switch to enable reporting of safety error. True : Safety error reporting is enabled. False: Safety error reporting is disabled. The detection of safety related errors is enabled by default to ensure that safety issues are addressed during the product lifecycle.
PARAMETER.PARAM_AutosarVersion: Applicable for Autosar versions 4.2.2, 4.4.0 and R24-11.

PARAMETER.PARAM_DESC: McalLibSpinlockTimeout is made as a Configuration Parameter, for the user to configure the spinlock timeout as per their requirements, to avoid the occurrence of the register write without acquiring spinlock. User shall configure the value of timeout and Spinlock will be acquired only within this specified timeout. But once this timeout occurs, the driver will update the register without acquiring spinlock and safety error "MCALLIB_E_TIMEOUT_FAILED" shall be reported.
PARAMETER.PARAM_AutosarVersion: Applicable for Autosar versions 4.2.2, 4.4.0 and R24-11.

The error code is reported if the API is invoked with a null pointer as a parameter.

ERROR.ERR_DESC: The error code is reported if the spinlock could not be acquired in the specified timeout.

ELEMENT.NAME: CPU: primary hardware peripheral
ELEMENT.DESC:
Hardware functional features The MCALLIB driver uses the CPU to retrieve the CPU ID on which the code is executing. The key hardware functional features used by the driver is:
  • CPU registers
The unsupported features of the CPU is:
  • Debug support
Users of the hardware The MCALLIB driver exclusively utilizes the CPU module. Hardware diagnostic features The SMU alarms configured for the CPU are not monitored by the MCALLIB driver. Hardware events Hardware events from CPU are not used by the MCALLIB driver.

ELEMENT.NAME: SCU: dependent hardware peripheral
ELEMENT.DESC: Hardware functional features The MCALLIB driver depends on the SCU IP for the clock functionality. The driver requires the fSPB and fSTM clock signals for functioning. ENDINIT feature of the SCU is implemented by the MCALLIB driver. Users of the hardware The SCU IP supplies clock for all the peripherals. The MCU driver is responsible for configuring the clock tree. To avoid conflicts due to simultaneous writes, update to all the ENDINIT protected registers is performed using the MCALLIB APIs. MCALLIB and WDG driver both update the WDT peripheral related registers. In order to avoid register corruption due to concurrent writes, all the writes to the WDT registers is performed under the same critical section by MCALLIB and WDG driver both. Hardware diagnostic features The SMU alarms configured for the SCU IP are not monitored by the MCALLIB driver. Hardware events Hardware events from the SCU are not used by the MCALLIB driver.

ELEMENT.NAME: STM: primary hardware peripheral
ELEMENT.DESC:
Hardware functional features The MCALLIB driver only reads the System Timer Bits [31:0]. The key hardware functional features used by the driver is:
  • Free-running system timer
The unsupported features of the STM is:
  • Compare match operation
Users of the hardware The MCALLIB driver provides API to read current STM tick count. Other MCAL driver uses the API for delay generation. Hardware diagnostic features Not applicable. Hardware events Hardware events from STM are not used by the MCALLIB driver.

HW_SW_INTERFACE.RESPONSIBILITIES: The MCAL Library (MCALLIB) provides a set of utility routines for use by the MCAL drivers. The services provided are ENDINIT management, global-local memory address translation, timer based delay, retrieval of CPU identifier, abstraction of TriCore-intrinsic instruction and spinlock.
HW_SW_INTERFACE.HW_SW_INTERFACE_DESC: This section describes the system view of the MCALLIB driver and peripherals administered by it.

EXPORTED_AOUS.TRUSTED_DESC: Product Cybersecurity claim is on top of functional safety claim. i.e. Integrator should fulfill safety AoUs along with cybersecurity AoUs to get cybersecurity claim. The following AoU shall be adhered to by the user of the McalLib driver:

TRUSTED_AOUS.TRUSTED_NAME: Access to shared registers by other drivers are trusted
TRUSTED_AOUS.TRUSTED_NOTES: Other drivers accessing shared registers for clock and password configurations shall be part of same level of trusted domain.

TRUSTED_AOUS.TRUSTED_NAME: McalLib executed from different trust domains
TRUSTED_AOUS.TRUSTED_NOTES: If McalLib is executed from different trust domains then the system integrator shall ensure that its global initialization is executed from the highest trust domain.

TRUSTED_AOUS.TRUSTED_NAME: Users or callers of McalLib in the same level of trust domain
TRUSTED_AOUS.TRUSTED_NOTES: McalLib APIs utilizing protected shared resources (e.g. shared global variables, CPU and SCU registers) which are invoked by other driver APIs (see granularity information in common UM) must be invoked in a trusted domain. Calls to such McalLib APIs from other drivers must not be made from untrusted cores.

TRUSTED_AOUS.TRUSTED_NAME: MCAL CooC - code and data to be protected
TRUSTED_AOUS.TRUSTED_NOTES: The system integrator shall ensure the confidentiality, integrity and availability of the MCAL CooC's code and data (volatile and non-volatile).

EXPORTED_AOUS.DESC: The AoU for the MCALLIB driver are as follows.

AOUS.NAME: ASIL level of calling module
AOUS.NOTES: Users shall ensure the FFI with respect to memory of modules invoking functions of MCALLIB, that have ASIL Level lower than that of MCALLIB.

AOUS.NAME: Common critical section
AOUS.NOTES: User shall ensure that core specific interrupts are disabled in the critical sections SchM_Enter_Wdg_CpuEndInit and SchM_Enter_McalLib_CpuEndInit.

AOUS.NAME: ENDINIT Protected Register Access
AOUS.NOTES: User shall ensure that all the ENDINIT protected registers are modified using only the write ENDINIT APIs (Mcal_WriteCpuEndInitProtReg, Mcal_WriteSafetyEndInitProtReg, Mcal_WriteSafetyEndInitProtRegMask, Mcal_WritePeripEndInitProtReg).

AOUS.NAME: Parameter range check for Mcal_SetBitAtomic and Mcal_GetBitAtomic
AOUS.NOTES: The MCALLIB user shall ensure the following while using the APIs Mcal_SetBitAtomic and Mcal_GetBitAtomic: - Sum of the input parameter BitPos and BitLen should not be greater than 32 bits - BitLen should always be constant and non-zero value

AOUS.NAME: Password check
AOUS.NOTES: User shall verify the password set by calling the GetPassword APIs (Mcal_GetCpuWdgPassword, Mcal_GetSafetyEndInitPassword, Mcal_GetPeripheralEndInitPassword) since the APIs related to setting of password does not authenticate the password and has no means to notify such an error.

AOUS.NAME: STM timer resolution
AOUS.NOTES: User shall call the Mcal_DelayResetTickCalibration API after any change in the clock tree to update the STM timer resolution.

AOUS.NAME: Test, Test and set spinlock mechanism
AOUS.NOTES:
User shall ensure that the lock address passed to the Mcal_Getspinlock() API must be at a non-cached memory address.
Mcal_Getspinlock() is called by MCAL modules: MCU, SMU and MCALLIB. Hence, the MCAL memory sections, MCU_17_TIMERIP_START_SEC_VAR_INIT_ASIL_B_GLOBAL_32, SMU_START_SEC_VAR_INIT_ASIL_B_GLOBAL_32 and MCALLIB_START_SEC_VAR_CLEARED_ASIL_B_GLOBAL_32 need to be placed in Non-Cache section.
(All functional safety modules use ASIL_B in their nomenclature. This need not be the safety level. Refer Release notes for the safety level of the respective module)
Note: There is a Timeout implemented within the Mcal_GetSpinlock Api and the user shall be aware that, if the spinlock (access to the register) is unavailable the function shall be blocking until the requested Timeout. Hence, recommended not to be used in ISRs.

AOUS.NAME: Valid address (base + offset) are passed as register address for McalLib API
AOUS.NOTES: Valid address (base + offset) shall be passed as the register address to the Mcal_WriteSafetyEndInitProtReg16 API.

AOUS.NAME: Valid CSFR address (only offset) are passed as register address for McalLib APIs
AOUS.NOTES: Valid CSFR address (only offset) shall be passed as the register address for Core Specific SFRs to the Mcal_WriteSafetyEndInitProtReg API

AOUS.NAME: Valid Pointer to be passed to APIs
AOUS.NOTES: User shall ensure the correctness of the pointer that is passed as an input parameter before invoking the MCALLIB APIs.

AOUS.NAME: Valid value are passed as parameter for MCALLIB APIs
AOUS.NOTES: User shall ensure the correctness of the data value that is passed as an input parameter before invoking the MCALLIB APIs.
